note: Per-case metadata that is not derived: the trap the pair was selected to probe, and the note that opens the case rationale. The rest of the rationale — which criterion drove the outcome — is appended by scripts/build_answer_key.py from the result of caliper.logic.roll_up, so it cannot disagree with the labels.
key_note: 51 cases over 8 trials and 14 patients. 36 are annotated: labelled criterion by criterion in two independent language-model passes and adjudicated by the maintainer, with the case outcome derived by applying caliper.logic.roll_up to the adjudicated criterion labels. 15 are constructed: an annotated pair with a recorded list of chart edits applied, the criteria those edits close overridden, and the outcome derived by the same rollup rule from the same human criterion labels. No clinician reviewed any of it, and no case outcome was written down by anyone reading the chart as a whole. The two provenances are reported separately everywhere. The finding behind the constructed cases: no patient in this corpus is eligible for any of these eight real protocols as their chart stands, because every protocol bounds at least one quantity no Synthea chart carries -- a liver panel for NCT01131676, a UACR for NCT02545049, NCT03819153 and NCT06717698, a cystatin C-based eGFR for NCT06717698, ECOG and RECIST and a brain MRI for NCT05748834, mMRC and pack-years and spirometry percent-predicted for NCT07252908, and an NYHA class for NCT03036124. Under the annotation protocol a test not done is unknown rather than normal, and unknown propagates. Every eligible case in this key is therefore constructed, and eval/annotation/protocol.md section 11 says exactly how.

cases.note: A recent, well-populated chart with type 2 diabetes and an in-range HbA1c: every demographic and metabolic criterion resolves, and the case still cannot be decided because the trial bounds liver enzymes this chart has never carried and the registry never defines its cardiovascular-risk criterion.
A clean inclusion failure on a chart current to two days before screening: prediabetes rather than type 2 diabetes, and an HbA1c below the trial's floor.

The chart carries a drug-misuse finding, but it is recorded as resolved in 2021 and the exclusion asks about the three months before consent. A matcher that reads the string without its status or its date fires an exclusion that should not fire.
The type 2 diabetes diagnosis is real and does not expire, but every measurement the protocol bounds is ten years old and no encounter has been recorded since 2016-06-13.
Sixty-five years of this patient's life are undocumented. The date of birth is the only fact that survives as usable.
Type 2 diabetes is present, but the trial wants diabetic kidney disease with high albuminuria and a maximal-dose RAAS blocker, and the chart has a normal UACR and no ACE inhibitor or ARB.
Serum potassium is exactly 4.80 mmol/L against a bound written as 4.8 mmol/L or below, so what the pair probes is whether that bound is read as inclusive. The case itself is decided elsewhere.
A diabetic kidney disease diagnosis with a ten-year-old UACR. The criterion asks for persistent albuminuria at the run-in and screening visits, and nothing in this chart can speak to either.
Three inclusions fail at once: no type 2 diabetes, no RAAS blocker, and a potassium of 4.97 mmol/L above the 4.8 mmol/L bound.

The chart has an ejection fraction, an NT-proBNP and an eGFR, and none of them is usable: the eGFR is MDRD reported in bare mL/min where the protocol names CKD-EPI in mL/min/1.73 m2, and all three are eleven years old.

An ejection fraction of 41.83% sits just above the trial's 40% ceiling and was measured in 1991. The pair exists to show that a threshold comparison against a thirty-five-year-old value is not a threshold comparison.
Established ischaemic heart disease and a chart current to 2026-05-30, but no heart failure and no heart-failure therapy, so the trial's core inclusion fails.
A two-year-old against an adult heart-failure trial. A key with no demographic floor cannot separate a system that checks age from one that does not.
The only pair in the key that satisfies this trial's diabetes inclusion, and it fails on renal function: an eGFR of 141.3 against a 25-60 window.
The same trial as AK-014 against a chart that stops in 2016. All five in-scope criteria are unresolved.
The absence of type 2 diabetes decides the case; the eGFR criterion is separately unresolvable because the reported value and the creatinine drawn the same day contradict each other.
Prediabetes and an HbA1c of 6.21% against a trial that requires type 2 diabetes at 7% or above.
The same shape as AK-017 on a different chart, kept so that the key is not carried entirely by its hard cases.
The shortest criterion set in the key against the emptiest chart in the corpus: five criteria, five unknowns.
Type 2 diabetes and an HbA1c inside range, but the renal band and the RAAS-blocker requirement both fail on values the chart does carry.

The renal inclusion cannot be evaluated at all: the protocol names creatinine-based CKD-EPI in mL/min/1.73 m2 and the chart reports MDRD in bare mL/min, a value that contradicts the creatinine measured the same day.
Prediabetes rather than type 2 diabetes and no RAAS blocker; the renal band is separately unresolvable because neither an eGFR nor a UACR has ever been measured.
A chart with exactly the right shape for a kidney trial — ACE inhibitor, ARB, sacubitril/valsartan — and no encounter for eleven years.

The oncology trial against a patient with no oncological history. The case-level answer is easy and the criterion-level answer is not: ECOG, RECIST, brain MRI, ejection fraction and a liver panel are not things this corpus contains, so most of the criteria are unknown.
The same trial against a female patient, which brings the pregnancy and sterilisation criteria into play. The diagnosis inclusions still decide it.

The oncology trial against a stale chart, selected because even the absence of breast cancer cannot be asserted here: seventeen of the nineteen criteria are unresolved, and the only inclusion that resolves is the age floor. What decides the case is the one exclusion that does resolve. Adjudication found that cystic fibrosis with pancreatic enzyme replacement is the malabsorption syndrome the trial's absorption exclusion names, and an active chronic diagnosis does not need the last decade to be documented. This is the only case in the key decided by an exclusion alone.
Every demographic and metabolic inclusion is met and the kidney trial still fails, on an eGFR above its ceiling and a UACR below its floor.
This trial admits participants without diabetes, so the chart clears its metabolic inclusions and fails on the absence of any ACE inhibitor or ARB.

A hypertensive patient on lisinopril 10 mg. Whether that is the maximum tolerated dose is not recorded, and neither an eGFR nor a UACR has ever been measured, so all three of the trial's renal-and-therapy inclusions are open.

The protocol asks for a creatinine-and-cystatin-C eGFR; cystatin C has never been measured here, and the creatinine-only value on file disagrees with the creatinine beside it. The case is decided by the missing RAAS blocker.
A 58-year-old woman whose chart ends in 1991. Almost every criterion is unresolved, including whether she is of childbearing potential.

FEV1/FVC is recorded as 66.607 % where the protocol writes the bound as a ratio below 0.7, and the trial's fasting-glucose bound is in mmol/L where every chart in the corpus records glucose in mg/dL. The case is decided by age.

An asthma diagnosis fires this COPD trial's concurrent-respiratory-disease exclusion, and the BMI ceiling and the COPD inclusions fail as well. Together with AK-026 it is one of only two cases in the key where an exclusion criterion fires at all.

Added after the first build to widen the base for the constructed cases, and annotated by both passes under the same protocol before any perturbation was written. Prediabetes rather than type 2 diabetes decides it, on a chart that has never carried a glomerular filtration rate.
